newsitem.title: USA: APPLIED MATERIALS LEADS GROUP RALLY.
newsitem.headline: APPLIED MATERIALS LEADS GROUP RALLY.

text.p: Shares in Applied Materials Inc posted sharp gains early Wednesday, leading a broad rally in semiconductor equipment stocks following the company's report late Tuesday of stronger than expected earnings.
Several Wall Street analysts quickly raised earnings estimates and ratings on Applied Materials, including Cowen & Co's Min Pang, who raised the stock to strong buy from buy.

In a research note, Pang said Applied Materials was benefitting from market share gains over its competitors, and therefore warranted a premium multiple to it peer group which is currently trading in a range of 20-22 times earnings.
"We are therefore using a 24-25 times calendar 1998 projection," Pang said, "to arrive at a target price of $115."
Some firms set sights even higher, including Salomon Brothers, which also raised the shares to strong buy with a $125 price target.

Robertson Stephens analyst Sue Billat, who kept a buy rating on the shares but raised earnings estimates for each of the next two years, said that while Applied Materials was apparently gaining share at the expense of competitors, there were positives in the company's results for the whole group.

"Revenues were higher than expected as several customers accelerated delivery schedules," Billat said. "We believe that this step-up in customer requirements is a positive indicator for Applied specifically and the semiconductor equipment industry in general."
Applied Materials, the largest of the chip equipment makers, earned $0.77 from operations in its third quarter, well above Wall Street's consensus view of $0.68 per share.
Applied Materials shares surged 7-7/8 to 98-1/8 at midday, the largest point gain among Nasdaq-listed shares.

Other semiconductor equipment companies that rallied included KLA-Tencor Corp, up 2-1/4 to 64-1/4, Kulicke & Soffa Industries Inc, up 1/2 to 42-3/4, Novellus Systems Inc up three to 110-3/8 and Teradyne Inc, up 2-5/8 to 49-3/8.
